title: vatica umbonata subsp. acrocarpa
intro: Vatica umbonata subsp. acrocarpa, commonly known as the Borneo ironwood, is a plant species within the family Dipterocarpaceae. It is traditionally used in Southeast Asian folk medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which help to alleviate symptoms of fever, diarrhea, and respiratory infections. The therapeutic actions of Borneo ironwood are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, that have antioxidant and immunomodulatory effects. Additionally, the plant has been used to treat wounds, snakebites, and other skin conditions due to its antiseptic and analgesic properties.
